thread:
maria: noticing some jitter when we batch-prefetch across tenant boundaries — if an eviction happens mid-batch we see a ~5-10ms tail per-request spike. anyone seen this and thought about making eviction batch-aware?

kai: seen it in perf traces, yes. batch formation can span prefixes that are about to be demoted. if we evict a prefix in the middle of a batch the KV miss forces an off-path fetch, breaking the whole batch.

sam: what's the proposal surface? do we stop evictions while a batch is in-flight? that sounds risky for memory storms. :thinking:

maria: not stop globally. idea: attach a small "batch-epoch" marker to requests and to prefix residency metadata. eviction would check epoch to avoid removing an in-flight prefix. cheap check.

lee: that preserves correctness but adds metadata. how much? per-prefix store: one int epoch + last-touched-epoch. per-request: 8 bytes. overhead seems acceptable, but need GC of stale epochs.

nina: also need to think about multi-node batches. if a batch spans nodes (coalescer), epoch must be propagated. we already tag requests with tenant id; add header `X-Batch-Epoch: <u64>` is straightforward.

maria: sketch: when batch is created, coordinator increments a monotonic epoch for that coalescing window and stamps requests. on eviction path: if prefix.residency_epoch >= request.batch_epoch -> treat as hot and skip eviction. else normal eviction.

kai: edge: what if prefix gets evicted and then reloaded under same epoch? we could see ABA. better: prefix should carry both residency_epoch and residency_generation. request carries (epoch, generation) and eviction checks generation equality to ensure monotonicity.

sam: generation makes it safer but increases complexity. also, how long do we pin prefixes? if batch waits behind queueing for too long we could artificially shield cold prefixes. need a TTL on batch-epochs.

lee: we can make epoch ephemeral: coordinator cleans epoch after N seconds (configurable). eviction logic uses epoch map + LRU: if epoch not found -> fall back to normal policy. small additional mem for epoch map keyed by epoch id -> timestamp.

nina: another tradeoff: this changes the lease invariant. our lease model currently assumes eviction is orthogonal to read batching. adding batch-awareness couples them. wonder about testing surface and fallout for long-lived cursors.

maria: agreed. propose minimal changes initially: 1) add batch_epoch tag on coordinator, 2) eviction checks existence of epoch and prefix residency epoch, 3) no generation for first iteration. If we see ABA replays in canary, promote generation.

sam: sounds pragmatic. what's rollback story? if this causes more binder memory, ops can reduce epoch TTL and we can fall back to previous eviction flag via runtime flag.

lee: also consider a different angle: instead of changing eviction, we could make batch coalescer conservative: avoid including recently-evicted candidate prefixes in new batches. cheaper since it keeps eviction unchanged.

maria: yes but coalescer conservatism loses batching opportunities. for high-throughput tenants that hurts p99s. I prefer eviction side guard.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: canary group A start at `infra/canary/kv-batch-epoch` - staged rollout + metrics.

nina: experiment plan: canary1 = 5% traffic for 6 hours, measure tail token latency, eviction rate, prefix residency churn, memory pressure. add a metric `batch_epoch_conflicts` to detect when eviction skipped due to epoch.

kai: add e2e test: simulate a batch that spans two prefixes, trigger eviction on one prefix mid-batch, assert no crash and no inconsistent reads. add microbench with synthetic workload to measure effect on batching hitrate.

maria: will draft the follow-up RFC short note with the tradeoffs + rollback. want reviewers: @kai, @sam, @lee. will post doc link later.

sam: lgtm for canary. make sure telemetry for epoch TTL is exposed so ops can tune.

lee: small nit: pick a compact encoding for epoch (u32) to avoid overindexing maps. and put default TTL = 2s.

maria: acknowledged. thanks all :rocket:
